title: Research sprint goal: Operations run as jobs a central queue places on workstation, server or CI executors
goal: (1) How does OPA sign, hash and verify a bundle, and which configuration gives it a bearer token_path and HS256 keys? (2) Which groups may own CODEOWNERS paths, and how deep do GitLab subgroups nest? (3) How does a GitLab pipeline trigger token pass variables or inputs, and what does the minimum role for pipeline variables refuse? (4) How does a headless claude -p choose between ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper and the subscription token? (5) What ends a Claude Code background command or a Monitor call, so a job must outlive the session that started it?
notes: No outside facts: the research landed before this story was filed, in commit 7d191fe8f (docs(kb): research OPA bundle signing, CODEOWNERS groups and pipeline triggers) and the kb's existing claude/ci-and-headless.md and claude/hooks.md facts; QK-operations-placement-stories-need-opa-bundles summarises it. Goal lead-in moved here: the sprint goal's open questions are answered with the kb tools first and the live docs for the gaps, and the findings are written as kb facts through the kb skills.
